finding.claim: OS command injection: the unsanitized `host` query parameter is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it via /bin/sh. Shell metacharacters (; | && $() backticks) allow arbitrary command execution as the server process user. The endpoint is unauthenticated and app.listen(3001) binds to all interfaces.
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, with the output returned to the attacker via res.send(out) at tools.js:11

trace.note: Public route GET /ping registered on the Express app with no auth middleware
req.query.host is concatenated directly into the command string and passed to exec(), which invokes a shell
Command stdout is returned in the response, so the attacker sees the output
app.listen(3001) with no host argument binds to all interfaces, so the endpoint is network-reachable

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist or regex on host. No authentication or authorization middleware. No use of execFile or an argument array, unlike /version at tools.js:16. exec's error callback only maps failures to 502 and does not mitigate. No rate limiting. Express can also deliver host as an array or object (e.g. ?host[]=a), which becomes a string via concatenation and does not block injection. Reproduction: curl 'http://TARGET:3001/ping?host=127.0.0.1;id' returns the output of `id` appended to the ping output. Fix: use execFile('ping', ['-c','1', host]) after validating host against a hostname/IP pattern, and reject values starting with '-'. Other routes checked: /version uses execFile with fixed args and no user input (not exploitable), and /uptime runs a fixed command (not exploitable). Neither is injectable.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec (shell) on the unauthenticated route at tools.js:6, with no validation, auth or middleware, and the output is returned at tools.js:11 on a server bound to all interfaces at tools.js:28.
